name: Political Refugee Status (Royal Decree) -- No Formal Asylum System

qualifying_event.description: Oman is not a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol, and has no national asylum law or administrative system for determining refugee status -- there is no Omani equivalent of an Asylum Office or standard refugee-status-determination procedure. All non-citizens, including asylum seekers, are governed by general immigration law (residence tied to work, investment, or family sponsorship -- see this dataset's other Oman routes). The one narrow exception: Oman's Foreign Residency Law contains a provision for 'political refugees,' whose status can be granted by Royal Decree at the Sultan's discretion. Article 36 of Oman's Constitution prohibits refoulement (forced return to persecution) as a general constitutional protection, independent of any asylum procedure.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: No standardized application or documentary process exists for the general population of asylum seekers; a political-refugee grant by Royal Decree is a discretionary, individual act of the Sultan rather than an applied-for status with defined evidentiary requirements.

requirement_groups.name: Political refugee status by Royal Decree

requirements.blocker_text: Status is granted at the Sultan's sole discretion by Royal Decree under a provision of the Foreign Residency Law -- there is no application process, eligibility test, or appeal mechanism available to the general public.

evidence_required.document: None -- no standard application exists; grant is a discretionary sovereign act

outcome.duration_length: not standardized -- no codified residence-card regime for asylum seekers or the general refugee population exists

sources.title: UNHCR Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform -- Oman is not a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention or 1967 Protocol; no national asylum law or RSD system exists; non-citizens fall under general immigration law; Foreign Residency Law contains a political-refugee-by-Royal-Decree provision; Article 36 of the Constitution prohibits refoulement; as of the data cited, Oman hosted 289 refugees and 415 asylum-seekers, most holding ordinary residence permits

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Oman). STATUS: DRAFT -- this file exists to document a genuine structural ABSENCE rather than to describe a workable, applied-for immigration route, consistent with this dataset's practice of disclosing gaps rather than fabricating process detail (see also Morocco's asylum-seeker-category gap built earlier in this dataset). The vast majority of the small recorded refugee/asylum-seeker population in Oman reportedly holds ordinary residence permits obtained through Oman's general immigration channels (work, investment, family) rather than through any refugee-specific status -- meaning a person fleeing persecution in practice depends on qualifying for one of this dataset's OTHER Oman routes (om_work_permit.json, om_family_reunification.json, etc.), not this one. work_rights, study_rights, and family_can_join are modeled 'none'/false specifically for the narrow, undefined political-refugee-by-decree status itself, not for asylum seekers generally, since no rights framework for that specific status was found described anywhere in the source reviewed.
